title: Bethel. El, yes: house of: Aleph, Beth
html_source:
Bethel is a stand-in for House of God where the ark of the covenant was kept (Gifford,p85). Bloom makes the connection and then rattles off the first two letters of the Hebrew alphabet, Aleph, Beth. This is another allusion to his Jewish ethnicity, which is part of his marginal identity, a persistent theme throughout the novel.

This also parallels a moment in Stephen’s monologue in “Proteus”, when he imagines making a phone call to the Garden of Eden. These occasional mental connections between both minds serve to highlight their affinities, what they have to learn from each other, while at the same time indicating certain fundamental differences—in this instance, Bloom’s Jewish and Hungarian background is set against Stephen’s own in Irish Catholicism; but the two are also linked in this, being both essentially secular people.
